milking of mankind, usury and the promotion of! 
enterprises intended to fleece the masses in their

namely food, clothing and shelter. 

Shanghai, as most of my listeners know, 


is a city dedicated to commerce and racketse 


Hoarding, profiteering, usury, and wildcat speculation 


have always played an important part in the economic 
life of the Asia Metropolis. This characteristic has

its 85 years of warped and hectic existencee The 
Sino-Japanese hostilities, of course, must be blamed 
as the root of this unhappy economic position. And 
like all wars, the Shanghai conflict had its crop of 


racketeers.

（印：SHANGHAI COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 22 AUG. 1939）

Further to attached report on the formation
of a "Shanghai Tenants' Association," Mr. J. H.
LACOUSTRA, a principal promoter of the organization
was interviewed by A.C. (Special Branch) at Police
Headquarters on the afternoon of August 21st when
the danger of holding an open meeting attended by
persons of all nationalities was pointed out to him.
As a result of this interview a meeting of
the organizers of the Association was held in
Mr. LACOUSTRA's flat No.45 Garden Apartment, 1173
Bubbling Well Road at 6 p.m., August 21st when the
advice of A.C. (Special Branch) regarding possible
disturbances leading to breaches of peace at the
mass meeting was discussed.
It was finally decided that the meeting would
be open to tenants of all nationalities but that no
representative of the landlords would be present.
No debates would be permitted.

（印章：上海总监办公室 1939年8月22日）

继附呈关于成立“上海房客协会”的报告之后，该组织的主要发起人 J. H. LACOUSTRA 先生于8月21日下午在警察总局接受了特别处助理总监（A.C.）的约谈，期间向其指出了举行有各国人士参加的公开会议的危险性。作为此次约谈的结果，协会组织者于8月21日下午6时在静安寺路1173号花园公寓45号 LACOUSTRA 先生的寓所举行会议，讨论了特别处助理总监（A.C.）关于群众集会可能引发骚乱并导致破坏治安的建议。

Date Jan. 4th, 1940

Subject: Re G.T. Lloyd's complaint re noisy work carried in Chinese shop
under his flat No. 4 at 374 Kiangse Road.
Made by Sub-Insp. Verkovsky Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

Re attached complaint, I beg to report that, accompanied by Sub-Insp. Hsu Shu Cheng, I interviewed the complainant Mr. G.T. Lloyd at his flat No. 4 at No. 374 Kiangse Road between 12.30 p.m. and 1 p.m. 4-1-40 and ascertained from him that the noisy work he complains of is allegedly carried out at all hours in the day and late through nights in a Chinese Machinery shop situated immediately under his flat, on the ground floor of the same building. This place was subsequently visited and found to be occupied by Messrs. Hun Sin Trading Corporation, 390 Kiangse Road (General Machinery Dealers).

The whole staff of that shop however, categorically denied carrying any noisy work.

They were nevertheless informed of the complaint lodged and strongly warned accordingly.

Inquiries were at the same time made at the Chung Hwa Machine Works Ltd. situated at No. 396 Kiangse Road, i.e. next door to the Hun Sin Trading Corp., but the staff there also denied carrying any noisy work, as well as stated having heard no noise having been made by their next door neighbours the Hun Sin Trading Corp.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
[Signature]
Sub-Inspector

主题：复 G.T. Lloyd 就其江西路374号4号寓所楼下中国店铺进行嘈杂作业提出的投诉。
呈报人：副督察 Verkovsky    转呈人：[签名]

先生，

关于附呈的投诉，谨报告如下：我于1940年1月4日中午12时30分至下午1时之间，会同副督察徐树成（Hsu Shu Cheng），在江西路374号4号寓所采访了投诉人 G.T. Lloyd 先生，并从他那里获悉，他所投诉的嘈杂作业据称在该楼底层、紧挨着他寓所下方的一家中国机器铺里日夜不停地进行的。随后我们走访了该处，发现其为汉兴贸易公司（Messrs. Hun Sin Trading Corporation，江西路390号，通用机械经销商）占用。

然而，该店全体员工断然否认进行任何嘈杂作业。

尽管如此，我们还是告知了他们已收到投诉，并据此给予了严厉警告。

同时，我们也向位于江西路396号、即汉兴贸易公司隔壁的中华机器厂有限公司（Chung Hwa Machine Works Ltd.）进行了查询，但该处员工也否认进行任何嘈杂作业，并表示未听到隔壁邻居汉兴贸易公司发出任何噪音。

此致，
敬礼，
[签名]
副督察

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No.
S. 5, Special Branch /316667,
REPORT
Date August 17, 1939.
Subject Broadcast made Mr. C.D. Alcott on Rent Racketeering.
Made by Cler. Asst. P. Tizon    Forwarded by Em Golan 28/

At 10.30 p.m. yesterday, Mr. C.D. Alcott,
speaking over Station XMA, delivered the following
address on rent racketeering in Shanghai :-

The three greatest curses of humanity are
war, cancer and the rackets. A racket, according to
the popular definition today is profiteering, the
milking of mankind, usury and the promotion of
enterprises intended to fleece the masses in their
struggle for the three prime economic wants of man,
namely food, clothing and shelter.

Shanghai, as most of my listeners know,
is a city dedicated to commerce and rackets.
Hoarding, profiteering, usury, and wildcat speculation
have always played an important part in the economic
life of the Asia Metropolis. This characteristic has
never been more pronounced than at the present time.
Shell-shocked, still suffering from the effects of
a war fought on our back doorsteps two years ago-
a war not yet over- it is not surprising that
Shanghai to-day should find itself confronted with
the most serious economic and financial situation of
its 85 years of warped and hectic existence. The
Sino-Japanese hostilities, of course, must be blamed
as the root of this unhappy economic position. And
like all wars, the Shanghai conflict had its crop of
racketeers.

（左侧页边批注/印章：FILE C 19）

昨晚10时30分，C.D. Alcott 先生通过 XMA 电台发表如下关于上海租金勒索问题的演讲：

人类的三大祸害是战争、癌症和勒索团伙。根据当今流行的定义，勒索团伙是指牟取暴利、榨取民脂民膏、高利贷以及推行旨在掠夺大众的企业，而大众正为人类三大基本经济需求，即食物、衣物和住所而挣扎。

正如大多数听众所知，上海是一座致力于商业和勒索团伙的城市。囤积居奇、牟取暴利、高利贷和盲目投机一直在这一亚洲大都市的经济生活中扮演重要角色。这一特征在当前时期表现得尤为明显。上海深受两年前在家门口进行的战争影响，震惊未消，且战争尚未结束，因此，上海在其85年扭曲而忙碌的历史中面临最严峻的经济和财政局势，这并不令人意外。当然，中日敌对行动必须被视为这一不幸经济状况的根源。像所有战争一样，上海冲突也滋生了一批勒索者。

（左侧页边批注/印章：归档 C 19）

(In that respect the Japanese Army is
unique because it carried with it its own profiteering
organ or what have you. The Special Section of the
Japanese Army is there specially to help the army to
live off the land by every means it can find. It is
only a so-called legitimate act of war. This has
extended itself to the area south of the Creek as well
as to the north of the Creek which is under Japanese
occupation).

Hoarding of food supplies by profiteers,
as a means of forcing the rank and file to pay better
prices later on, has been one of the most vicious
rackets to exist in this city. At the moment,
Shanghai is actually confronted with a rice famine and
hoarders, still dealing in native rice, are holding
their stocks of superior quality grain, selling
inferior grades at top prices. Before the present
rice situation has clarified itself, the Settlement
authorities may find it necessary to take new action
toward control. In fact, a meeting on this very topic
was held by the gentlemen of the S.M.C. Tuesday.
Action was deferred.

However, there is still another racket,
now being operated in the foreign administered areas
of Shanghai and no control is yet in sight. It is a
far more serious racket than the rice situation,

（在这方面，日军是独特的，因为它携带了自己的牟利机构或类似组织。日军特务机关专门在那里帮助军队通过各种手段就地补给。这仅仅是一种所谓的合法战争行为。这种行为已扩展到浜南地区以及被日军占领的浜北地区）。

投机商囤积粮食供应，以此迫使普通民众日后支付更高价格，这是本市存在的最恶劣的勒索行为之一。目前，上海实际上正面临米荒，囤积者仍在交易国产大米，他们持有优质谷物库存，却以最高价格出售劣质大米。在目前大米局势明朗化之前，租界当局可能发现有必要采取新的管制措施。事实上，上海公共租界工部局 (S.M.C.) 的绅士们周二就这一主题举行了会议。行动被推迟。

然而，在上海的外国管理区域还有另一种勒索行为正在运作，目前尚无管制迹象。这是一种比大米局势更严重的勒索行为，

primarily because the Council will, if pushed, control
the rice problem. I am referring to the rent racket.
With the exception of a very small minority of foreigners
who receive their incomes in foreign currency, these
rackets are working a hardship on the great bulk of
the population of the International Settlement and
the French Concession, that may have more serious
repercussions than those engaged in their operation
perhaps realize at the moment.
        Apparently, some of our landlords, their
vision blurred by quick and fantastic profits, have
lost their balance. For nothing would please the
Japanese more than to see the foreign and Chinese
vested interests in the foreign areas engaged in a tong
war with the public on the question of rent profiteering
or any other big economic squeeze. Such an economic
disturbance in the foreign concessions, at the present
time, would be the instrument of propaganda the
Japanese have been waiting for-propaganda they could
use in winning over the Chinese masses to their side
of the fence. An empty stomach and no place to sleep
are powerful instruments of persuasion.
        Don't think that I am giving the Japanese
any new ideas. ""ayor" Fu Siao-an, of the Japanese
sponsored regime, has already started such a propaganda
campaign. Just how far he is going to get with it

主要是因为如果受到压力，工部局将控制大米问题。我指的是租金勒索。除了极少数收入为外币的外国人外，这些勒索行为给国际租界和法租界的大部分人口带来了困难，其后果可能比从事这些操作的人目前意识到的更为严重。
        显然，我们的一些房东被快速且惊人的利润冲昏了头脑，失去了理智。没有什么比看到外国区域内的外国和中国既得利益者在租金牟利或其他重大经济压榨问题上与公众发生帮派战争更让日本人高兴的了。目前外国租界的这种经济动荡，将是日本人一直等待的宣传工具——他们可以利用这种宣传来争取中国民众站在他们一边。空空的肚子和无栖身之所是强有力的说服工具。
        不要以为我在给日本人出新主意。日本扶植政权的“市长”傅筱庵已经开始了这样的宣传运动。他能走多远

depends entirely on how far the landlord south of
Soochow Creek is willing to go to meet his tenants half
way.

I know that some landlords listening to
this bit of conversation can talk all afternoon about
maintenance costs, depreciation and the low interest
they are receiving on their investments. They can
howl for hours over the sad state of the foreign
exchange market and the low value of the Chinese dollar.
They quote figures to prove they are losing out all the
way. And some of them probably feel just
as miserable as they sound. But what some of them
don't seem to realize, and what some tenants do not
seem to understand is that they are all lucky to be
in business in Shanghai at the present time, considering
everything else that has happened in the Far East
during the past two years.

I know that some tenants can be
unreasonable and I also am well aware that there are
two kinds of landlords. For instance, I know a
landlord, running a modern office building in the
Central District, who hasn't raised his rents since
1934. Right now, he is making less than one-tenth
of one per cent on his investment. However, he feels
lucky to be able to break even. Landlords like this
fellow are rarities in Shanghai at the moment, but

完全取决于苏州河以南的房东愿意在多大程度上向房客妥协。

我知道有些听这段谈话的房东可以整个下午谈论维护成本、折旧以及他们投资获得的低利息。他们可以连续几个小时哀叹外汇市场的悲惨状况和中国货币的低价值。他们引用数据证明他们一直在亏损。其中一些人可能真的像他们听起来那样痛苦。但有些人似乎没有意识到，而有些房客似乎也不理解的是，考虑到过去两年远东发生的其他一切事情，他们能在上海继续经营已是幸运之事。

我知道有些房客可能不讲道理，我也很清楚房东有两种类型。例如，我认识一位在中央区经营现代化办公楼的房东，自1934年以来从未涨过租金。目前，他的投资回报率不到千分之一。然而，他觉得能保本已是幸运。像这样的人在上海目前是凤毛麟角，但

even he must raise his rents as a result of the
continued drop in the exchange. He tells me that
he plans a hike of not more than 30 per cent in native
currency. None of his tenants can kick about that;
can kick over a 30 per cent increase on the rent they
were paying five years ago.

This is not the fellow I am talking about
tonight. He is way in the minority, as far as the
general run of Shanghai landlords go.

The chap I am talking about is the
individual who goes on a gold or pound sterling basis
and tells his tenants to take it or leave it; the
fellow who tries to throw tenants out because he has
some one on the string who is willing to pay a bigger
rental; the man who spends his nights trying to figure
out how to break leases and chuck his tenants out on
their ears in the morning; the individual who wants
to create a new standard of currency in Shanghai for
himself and to hell with the other fellow.

This is the individual, he and his kind,
who are in the majority in Shanghai at the moment.
This is the rent racketeer, the man whose activities
the Shanghai Municipal Council says it cannot control

I am not challenging the statement on this
subject issued by the Council recently. But I would

即使是他，由于汇率持续下跌，也必须提高租金。他告诉我，他计划以本国货币涨幅不超过30%。他的房客对此无可抱怨；毕竟，这只是比五年前支付的租金增加了30%。

这不是我今晚要谈的那个人。就上海房东的整体情况而言，他是极少数。

我要谈的是那种坚持按黄金或英镑计价，告诉房客要么接受要么滚蛋的人；是那种因为有人愿意支付更高租金而试图赶走房客的人；是那种整夜绞尽脑汁想办法破坏租约、第二天早上把房客扫地出门的人；是那种想为自己在上海建立新货币标准、不管别人死活的人。

这种人及其同类目前在上海占多数。这就是租金勒索者，上海公共租界工部局称其无法控制其活动的人。

我并不挑战工部局近期就此主题发表的声明。但我希望

- 6 -

like to point out that while there may be nothing in
the land regulations of the International Settlement
specifically providing for the control of rentals,
there is a provision providing for action in time of
emergency. And it is not stretching the truth to
state that the present rental ramps being worked on
a tired, nerve wracked, miserable Shanghai public
constitute a definite emergency. Hongkong chose to
regard rental rackets in that city as being serious
enough to demand action and action was taken. But why
doesn't the Council take some action, why does it
attempt to slip out of the current rental war by
maintaining that its hands are tied?
        The answer is simple. The Council is
collecting taxes on these increased rentals. For
instance, I know of no end of one and two room
apartments renting for rates from $65 to $100 before
the outbreak of hostilities in 1937, that are now
going for rentals ranging from U.S. $25 to U.S. $30,
or a 300 per cent increase at today's rate of exchange.
The S.M.C. collects taxes on these rentals at the old
rate of 12 per cent. And that is good business for
the Council. The S.M.C. at the moment needs all the
money it can get. I don't deny that but living in
Shanghai today is a case of give and take and the small
boy can't go on forever doing most of the giving.

谨指出，虽然《国际租界土地章程》中可能没有任何具体规定用于管控租金，但其中有一项条款规定了在紧急情况下采取行动。如果说目前猖獗的租金勒索行为正在折磨着疲惫、神经衰弱、痛苦的上海公众，从而构成明确的紧急情况，这并非夸大其词。香港选择将该市的租金勒索团伙视为严重到需要采取行动的问题，并确实采取了行动。但是，为什么工部局不采取一些行动？为什么它试图通过声称束手无策来逃避当前的租金战争？
        答案很简单。工部局正从这些增加的租金中征收税款。例如，据我所知，无数的一室和两室公寓在1937年战事爆发前的租金为65至100美元，而现在的租金则为25至30美元（按今日汇率计算），增幅达300%。上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）按旧的12%税率对这些租金征税。这对工部局来说是一笔好生意。目前，上海公共租界工部局需要尽其所能获取资金。我不否认这一点，但在今天的上海生活是一种相互妥协的过程，小人物不能永远承担大部分付出。

- 7 -

Eventually, he is going to get tired and move out. He
is better off back home where some control is exercised
over profiteers. And if he does move out what will
happen. Shanghai will be left to the Japanese and the
landlords. And in the ensuing scrap, no one needs to
be told who will win. It won't be the landlords.
        I am not talking about the many ramifications
of the rent question in Shanghai tonight because it would
take more time than I have at my disposal. But you can
believe me when I say that I can quote case after case
of pure unadulterated rent racketeering that would make
your head swim. I may do it Saturday night and mention
a few names just for fun. At the same time, I can
name a few landlords who realize the broader aspects of
the situation and have exercised some restraint in
dealing with their tenants. These people know that
if the foreign areas survive the present troublous times
in China, that they will still be in business, will still
be collecting rents. They know that the two and one
half million Chinese refugees in Shanghai today will
be gone, at least most of them. They also know that
Shanghai is perhaps the only foreign administered
city in the world where the landlord gets a break that
he could not possibly expect elsewhere. He doesn't pay
the taxes. His tenants pay them but that doesn't
prevent him from keeping his rents up.

最终，他会感到厌倦并搬离。回到家乡对他更好，因为那里对发国难财者有一定的管制。如果他真的搬走，会发生什么？上海将留给日本人和房东。在随后的争斗中，无需告知谁将获胜。获胜者不会是房东。
        我今晚不谈上海租金问题的许多复杂方面，因为这会占用比我现有更多的时间。但请相信我，我可以列举一个个纯粹且毫无掩饰的租金勒索案例，足以让你头晕目眩。我可能会在周六晚上这样做，并为了好玩提及几个名字。同时，我也能点名几位意识到局势更广泛层面并在对待租户时有所克制的房东。这些人知道，如果外国管辖区在中国目前的动荡时期幸存下来，他们仍将继续经营，继续收取租金。他们知道，目前在上海的250万中国难民将会离开，至少大部分人会离开。他们还知道，上海也许是世界上唯一一个由外国人管理的城市，在那里房东能得到他在其他地方不可能指望的优待。他不缴纳税款。他的租户缴纳，但这并不妨碍他维持高租金。

I suppose some Shanghai officials might
want to give me an argument about my statement claiming
that there are two and a half million war refugees in
Shanghai. For months, S.M.C. and French officials have
been boasting how little they have been troubled with
the refugee problem They only have, according to their
figures, some forty or fifty thousand persons in their
refugee camps. Such figuring is completely haywire.
I wonder who the authorities think these people who have
caused all this congestion in the Settlement and the
French Concession really are if not refugees. The only
difference between them and those in the camps is that
the latter have no money and are objects of charity.

In view of the trouble that has arisen
between tenants and landlords over the present rental
question, it strikes me that there is only one immediate
solution, namely that the case of the tenants must be
taken considerably higher than the Shanghai Municipal
Council, namely the Consular Body and the various
Embassies concerned, unless, of course, the landlords
are willing to give away some ground and the tenants
are willing to do likewise. I know one large real
estate company that is collecting one-third of its
rent in pounds sterling and the other two-thirds in
local currency. This sounds to me like a reasonable
solution. It enables the landlord to meet his
commitments abroad, his plumbing and elevator repairs

我想，一些上海官员可能会对我关于上海有250万战争难民的说法提出争论。几个月来，上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）和法国当局一直吹嘘他们在难民问题上受到的困扰多么少。根据他们的数据，他们的难民营中只有四五万人。这种计算完全混乱不堪。我想知道，如果不是难民，当局认为这些造成租界和法租界如此拥挤的人究竟是谁？他们与难民营中的人的唯一区别在于，后者没有钱，是慈善救济的对象。

鉴于目前因租金问题而在租户和房东之间产生的纠纷，我认为只有一个直接的解决方案，即租户的案件必须提交到比上海工部局更高的层级，即领事团和相关各国大使馆，除非房东愿意做出一些让步，且租户也愿意这样做。我知道一家大型房地产公司收取三分之一的英镑租金和三分之二的本地货币租金。这在我看来是一个合理的解决方案。它使房东能够履行其在海外的承诺，支付管道和电梯维修费用

- 9 -

and other costs and at the same time, removes much
hardship from the shoulders of the tenant. It is
unfortunate that several other leading real estate
firms have not seen fit to follow this company's lead.
    But if the tenants are going to get any
action, they cannot expect to achieve much as individuals
or small units. It requires organization, definite
organization that can be maintained perhaps on a
permanent basis. Attempts have already been made to
form such an organization but they have not progressed
to any great extent because a good many felt that it
might be another gyp racket, or because they were
afraid to make themselves heard; afraid of their jobs.
There is too much of that sort of thing in Shanghai;
too many people afraid to 'air their grievances because
the boss is like to turn them out in the cold the next
morning.
    However, I have noticed during the past
few weeks, as a result of the sky-rocketing living
costs that discontent among the Shanghai masses has
reached such a state that the average man working for
vested interests doesn't care much whether school
keeps or not; is just about ready to throw up the
sponge and travel back home, even if he has to take
a rowboat. It is my contention that now is the ideal
time to organize a tenants' association in Shanghai

及其他成本，同时也减轻了租户的大部分负担。不幸的是，其他几家领先的房地产公司认为不宜效仿这家公司的做法。
    但是，如果租户想要获得任何行动成果，他们不能指望作为个人或小团体取得多大成就。这需要组织，明确的可维持的组织，或许可以建立在永久基础上。已经有人尝试组建这样的组织，但进展不大，因为许多人觉得这可能又是另一个诈骗勾当，或者因为他们害怕发声；害怕丢掉工作。上海这类事情太多了；太多人不敢“发泄不满”，因为老板很可能第二天早上就让他们卷铺盖走人。
    然而，在过去几周里，我注意到，由于生活成本飞涨，上海民众的不满情绪已达到这样一种状态：那些为既得利益集团工作的普通人不太在乎学校是否开学；几乎准备放弃努力回老家，即使不得不坐划艇回去。我的观点是，现在是在上海组织租户协会的理想时机

Subject Shanghai General Chamber of Commerce: scale of fees for arbitration
in rent disputes.
Made by D.F.S. Roberts. Forwarded by ____

〔左侧手写签名：Thos Roberts〕

〔左侧椭圆印章：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE / 27 SEPT. 1939〕

〔左侧手写批注：28/9〕

Concerning the attached newspaper report
published in the China Press on September 24, 1939,
Mr. Swan, joint secretary of the Shanghai General
Chamber of Commerce was interviewed during the
morning of September 25, 1939.

Mr. Swan stated that the committee of the
above Chamber met to consider the means of defraying
the cost of running the Arbitration Board and decided
that certain fees be levied for the proceedings taken
by the Board (a printed form issued by the Chamber
containing the scale of fees is attached hereto
together with a copy of the agreement signed by the
disputants before negotiations are commenced).

In the course of the interview Mr. Swan
pointed out that the scale of fees agreed upon com-
pared favourably with those adopted by Committees of
a similar nature in other branches of the business.

Owing to the attached newspaper report
being published, Mr. Swan is calling a meeting of
the committee to discuss whether the fees can be
lowered, but he is of the opinion, that unless the
arbitrators are prepared to offer their services
free of charge no change can be made.

The Committee, during their last meeting,
concluded that so far as could be seen the only
people likely to make use of the Arbitration Board
would be groups of tenants residing in apartment
buildings who could divide the cost between them.

〔左侧手写批注：9月28日〕

关于1939年9月24日刊登在《字林西报》上的所附报纸报道，上海总商会联合秘书Swan先生于1939年9月25日上午接受了问询。

Swan先生表示，上述商会的委员会开会讨论了支付仲裁委员会运行费用的方法，并决定对委员会采取的程序收取某些费用（随函附上商会发布的包含收费标准的印刷表格，以及争议双方在谈判开始前签署的协议副本）。

在问询过程中，Swan先生指出，商定的收费标准与其他商业领域的类似性质委员会采用的标准相比具有优势。

由于刊登了所附的报纸报道，Swan先生正在召集委员会会议讨论是否可以降低费用，但他认为，除非仲裁员愿意免费提供服务，否则无法做出任何改变。

委员会在上次会议中得出结论，就目前所见，唯一可能使用仲裁委员会的人群将是居住在公寓楼中的租户群体，他们可以在彼此之间分摊费用。

same before the expiration of two weeks from the date hereof, or before such other date as
the arbitrators shall by writing endorsed hereon fix for making such award, and in case the
said two arbitrators do not make and publish their award within the time so to be appointed
by them, the said umpire shall make and publish his award or umpirage within such time as
he shall by writing endorsed hereon appoint, with power to him from time to time by writing
endorsed hereon to enlarge the time so appointed by him.

3.—The arbitrators or umpire shall have power to award payment of the costs, fees, and
expenses incurred in the arbitration, but the fees payable to them as such arbitrators or
umpire shall not exceed that laid down in the scale published from time to time by the
Shanghai General Chamber of Commerce.

4.—The submission hereby made shall not be defeated or affected by the death of either
of the parties hereto, pending the same, but shall or may be proceeded in, and the matters in
difference determined in the same manner as if the award had been made or determined in
the lifetime of the party or parties so dying.

5.—The arbitrators or umpire shall at liberty to proceed ex parte, in case either party,
after reasonable notice, shall at any time neglect or refuse to attend on the reference, without
having previously shown to the said arbitrators or umpire what the latter shall consider good
and sufficient cause for omitting to attend.

6.—The parties hereto shall respectively produce before the arbitrators or umpire all
books, deeds, papers, documents, vouchers, writings, and documents within their possession
or control which the arbitrators or umpire may require and call for as in their judgment
relating to the matters referred to, and the arbitrators or umpire may dispense entirely or in
part with verbal evidence, and may require from each party a statement in writing supporting
his case and may decide the arbitration on such written statement.

2. 两名仲裁员应以书面形式作出裁决，并由他们正式签署，该裁决应准备交付给本协议各方，或其中希望获得裁决的任何一方，交付时间不得晚自本协议日期起两周届满之前，或不晚于仲裁员通过在此背书的书面文件所确定的作出该裁决的其他日期；如果上述两名仲裁员未在他们如此指定的时间内作出并公布其裁决，则上述公断人应在其通过在此背书的书面文件所指定的时间内作出并公布其裁决或公断，并有权通过在此背书的书面文件不时延长其所指定的时间。

3. 仲裁员或公断人有权裁定支付仲裁过程中产生的费用、酬金和开支，但作为仲裁员或公断人应付给他们的酬金不得超过上海总商会不时公布的费率表中所规定的限额。

4. 任何一方当事人在待决期间死亡，不应导致或影响 hereby 作出的提交仲裁之效力，而应或可以继续进行，并以如同在该方或诸方去世生前已作出裁决或判定的相同方式判定争议事项。

5. 如果任何一方在收到合理通知后，在任何时候忽视或拒绝出席仲裁程序，且此前未向上述仲裁员或公断人说明后者认为正当且充分的缺席理由，则仲裁员或公断人有权进行单方审理。

6. 本协议各方应分别向仲裁员或公断人出示由其占有或控制的所有账簿、契据、文件、单据、凭证、文书及文档，凡仲裁员或公断人认为与提交事项相关并要求提供的，均须出示；仲裁员或公断人可以完全或部分免除口头证据，并可要求各方提供支持其主张的书面陈述，并可根据该书面陈述对仲裁作出决定。

CHINA PRESS
SEP 24 1938

Tenant Body
Will Aid Rent
Settlement

Group May Prosecute
Before Arbitration
Board Here

Sentiment is growing here for a
Shanghai Tenant Associa-
tion to combat the solution of
the local rent problem started with
formation of the General Chamber
of Commerce Arbitration Board re-
cently. A step in the direction of
united tenantry will be an early
convention of Association members,
it was learned yesterday.
Published at the request of the
S.M.C., the Arbitration board's
formation was announced some
weeks ago. Later it was learned
that fees of the board would pro-
hibit small tenants from taking ad-
vantage of the opportunity to com-
bat the exorbitant rent demands
made by landlords here. It was
then that renewed interest was
aroused in the Tenants Association
which at one time appeared
moribund.
Charges of the arbitration board
will be an initial $14 for the Cham-
ber of Commerce and $21 apiece for
two arbiters and an umpire for the
first hour of their labors and $10.50
apiece for each hour thereafter.
Thus a case which occupied a
morning would cost two or three
hundred dollars all of which would
presumably be paid by the tenant
who appeared as complainant.
A panel of arbitrators have been
appointed by the Chamber. When
a case is brought for settlement
two members of the panel will be
chosen for duty and they in turn
will choose an umpire. Names of
those composing the panel have not
been disclosed.

Problem Is Civic

While many interested people
agree that the Chamber has a right
to charge a fee they are inclined
to look on the entire matter as one
of wide enough proportions to as-
sume civic importance. At any rate,
although there are a considerable
number of controversial rent cases
in the city, none of them have yet
been brought before the board pro-
bably because of the cost involved.
This is where the Tenants As-
sociation enters the picture. If it
can collect enough funds from a
large enough membership, it will
be able to fight many of the battles
of members and help materially to
combat the rent evil.
Leaders of the movement
visualize a group of 1,000 or more
paying $12 per year. Already early
members have contributed large
sums but these have been irregular
and insufficient for carrying any
cases to court.
Before the forthcoming meeting,
however, officers of the Association
expect to have vital issues of the
rent situation selected for discus-
sion. One of these is the matter
of who can be made ultimately re-
sponsible for exorbitant increases.
This problem arises from the fact
that many Chinese owners place
their property in the hands of
foreign firms who cannot be made
responsible for policies regarding
the dwellings.

《字林西报》（China Press）
1938年9月24日

租户团体
将协助租金
和解

该团体可能在此间
仲裁委员会前
提起诉讼

据悉，此处要求成立上海租户协会以应对当地租金问题的呼声日益高涨，此举始于最近上海总商会仲裁委员会的成立。据昨日获悉，迈向租户联合的一步将是协会成员尽早召开大会。

应工部局（S.M.C.）的要求发布，仲裁委员会的组建于数周前宣布。后来得知，该委员会的费用将使小租户无法利用这一机会来对抗本地房东提出的过高租金要求。正是在那时，人们对租户协会重新产生了兴趣，该协会曾一度显得奄奄一息。

仲裁委员会的收费为：总商会收取初始费用14美元，两名仲裁员和一名公断人在第一小时工作时间内每人收取21美元，此后每小时每人收取10.50美元。因此，一个占用一上午时间的案件将花费两三百美元，所有这些费用 presumably 将由作为申诉人的租户支付。

总商会已任命了一个仲裁员小组。当案件提交解决时，将从小组中选出两名成员履行职责，他们再选择一名公断人。组成该小组的人员名单尚未披露。

问题具有市政性质

虽然许多感兴趣的人同意总商会有权收取费用，但他们倾向于将整个事件视为具有足够广泛的比例从而具备市政重要性。无论如何，尽管本市存在相当数量的有争议的租金案件，但尚无案件提交至该委员会，这可能是因为涉及的成本。

这正是租户协会介入之处。如果它能从足够多的会员那里筹集到足够的资金，它将能够为会员打赢许多官司，并在实质上帮助对抗租金弊端。

该运动的领导者设想拥有一个由1,000名或更多每年缴纳12美元的会员组成的团体。早期会员已经捐赠了大笔款项，但这些捐款并不规律，且不足以支撑任何案件进入法庭。

然而，在即将召开的会议之前，协会负责人期望选出租金局势的关键问题进行讨论。其中之一是谁最终应对过高的涨幅负责的问题。这一问题产生于这样一个事实：许多中国业主将其房产置于外国公司手中，而这些公司无法对有关住房的政策负责。

制作人：D.P.S. Roberts    转呈人：R G Black (x)

关于附件中刊登于1939年9月14日《字林西报》（North China Daily News）和《上海泰晤士报》（Shanghai Times）上提及上海总商会仲裁租金纠纷的报告，于9月14日下午在外滩17号办公室采访了总商会联合秘书 SWAN 先生。

SWAN 先生表示，上述组织已接到公共租界和法租界当局的接洽，并被请求承担解决房东与租户之间纠纷的工作。

9月12日，上海总商会委员会召开会议，决定了以下程序：

从公正无私的人士中选定一个仲裁员小组，在收到援助申请后，将从小组中指派两名成员处理案件并作出决定。

在开始任何程序之前，被选定的人员将提名另一名成员作为公断人，该公断人将获知所有事实等，如果两名仲裁员在任何问题上意见不一，将征求他的决定，并将其视为最终决定。

任何租户、租户团体或房东，无论国籍如何，均可提交申请。

委员会决定，对于争议在于租金是否应以非中国货币支付的案件，应提交给有关法院，因为外国法院尚未就此作出裁决。

SEP 1 3 1939

Commerce Body
Meets To Form
Rent Board

A committee of the General
Chamber of Commerce last night
reaffirmed the organization's deter-
mination to form a rent adjustment
body here and then discussed the
general procedure to be used in
settling rent disputes.
Although the meeting formulated
no definite rules and adjourned to
a later date this week, certain prin-
ciples were fixed upon for the
technique of arbitration to be used.
In each dispute between landlord
and tenant an absolutely impartial
panel drawn from members of the
Chamber will decide the merits of
the case. The panels will be
chosen by the disputants from a
prepared list of names.
The Chamber agreed to assume
responsibility for formation of an
adjustment committee some time
ago following a request from the
Shanghai Municipal Council.

虽然会议没有制定明确的规则，并休会至本周稍后日期，但就拟使用的仲裁技术确定了一些原则。

在每一起房东与租户的纠纷中，一个从商会成员中抽选的绝对公正的小组将裁定案件的实质。该小组将由争议双方从一份预备名单中选择。

Dispute between Japanese tenants and Cathay Land Company.

Note by D. S. Kamashita. Forwarded by D. I. Crawford.

With reference to the attached extracts from local English dailies regarding the dispute between Japanese tenants and the Cathay Land Company, located in the Sassoon House, I have to state that towards the middle of December, 1939, tenants occupying flats of the Chanchun Road Apartments, Dixwell Apartments, and Apartments at the corner of Dixwell and North Szechuen Roads, which have steam heating were notified by the authorities of the Cathay Land Company, the owners of those apartments, that the house rent would be raised by 35% with effect from January, 1940, on account of the high cost of fuel, etc.

The Japanese tenants numbering 120 are of the opinion that an increase is justifiable but that the above percentage is too high. A mass meeting of the Japanese tenants was held at the Japanese Church on Darroch Road at 5 p.m. January 13. Mr. K. Sugimoto presided over the meeting when five members of the executive committee including Mr. Sugimoto, were elected. The above committee will negotiate with the authorities of the company regarding the new increase in rentals.

D. S. Kamashita

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS

Nippon Women
Oppose New
Rental Hikes

Leaving their pots and pans behind, woman tenants of three apartment houses in north Hongkew came out of their kitchens Saturday to attend a mass meeting against a 35 per cent raise in rents imposed upon them by the Sassoon-controlled Cathay Land Company, the Tairiku Shimpo reported yesterday.

Presided over by Mr. Kyutaro Sugimoto, the mass meeting held at the Japanese Christian Church on Darroch Road voted in favor of organizing a tenants' union to fight the increase in rentals. An executive committee consisting of five members, elected at the mass meeting, was scheduled to meet at 1 o'clock yesterday afternoon to discuss steps to be taken, the Japanese daily stated.

Affected by the raise are 120 occupants of the apartments located above the Shanghai Co-operative Society, North Szechuen and Dixwell Roads; the Changchun Road Apartments, and the Dixwell Road Apartments.

受此次涨价影响的有120名住户，他们居住在位于北四川路与狄思威路上海协进会社上方的公寓、春阳路公寓以及狄思威路公寓。

pages.en:
Miscellaneous 312/39
Hongkew Station
October 24th, 1939.

Further report on complaint against D.P.S. 809 F. Masuda lodged
by Mrs. Samuel Goldstein, owner of "Rooming Houses" situated at
Quinsan Gardens.

Sir,

Mrs. Samuel Goldstein accompanied by her mother Mrs.
Levy came to Hongkew Station about 3.30 p.m. on October
24th, 1939 and was interviewed by the undersigned with reference
to a letter in Japanese, which she received from her Japanese
tenants per registered post on October 21st, 1939. A copy of
the translation of it made by "Tanaka Interpreter-negotiator Service",
Range Road, on October 23rd, 1939 is attached herewith.

It will be noted from the letter that the Japanese
tenants of the "Rooming Houses" at Quinsan Gardens, owned by
Mrs. Samuel Goldstein, reject her demand regarding the raising
of the rentals and also included are suggestions with reference to
the betterment of the conditions of the rooms occupied by them.
Mrs. S. Goldstein, consequently went on the afternoon of October
24th, 1939 to see Mr. H.H. Thomas, Consul for Japanese Affairs at
H.B.M. Consulate with reference to it; He on seeing it advised
her to interview Mr. H. Umekawa at the Japanese Consulate also show
the letter to the Police at Hongkew for record, hence the reason
for the report and copy attached.

I am, Sir,

Yours obediently,

Sugita A. TELFER.
Det. Insp.

1939年10月24日。

关于昆山路花园（Quinsan Gardens）“出租房屋”业主塞缪尔·戈尔茨坦夫人（Mrs. Samuel Goldstein）对 D.P.S. 809 F. Masuda 提出的投诉的进一步报告。

先生，

塞缪尔·戈尔茨坦夫人在其母亲利维夫人（Mrs. Levy）的陪同下，于1939年10月24日下午3时30分左右来到虹口分局，就她于1939年10月21日通过挂号信收到的日本租户来信一事接受了本人的问询。随函附上由“田中翻译-谈判服务处”（Tanaka Interpreter-negotiator Service，位于兰路）于1939年10月23日制作的译文副本。

从信中可以看出，昆山路花园“出租房屋”的日本租户（该房产由塞缪尔·戈尔茨坦夫人所有）拒绝了她关于提高租金的要求，并且信中还包括了关于改善他们所居住房间条件的建议。因此，S. 戈尔茨坦夫人于1939年10月24日下午就此事宜去拜见了英国驻沪总领事馆日本事务领事 H.H. 托马斯先生（Mr. H.H. Thomas）；他在查看信件后建议她也去会见日本领事馆的梅川 H. 先生（Mr. H. Umekawa），并将信件出示给虹口警方以备记录，故此呈报并附上副本。

此致，

您顺从的仆人，

Sugita A. TELFER.
侦探督察。

Translation.

Oct. , 1938.

Mr. J... Levy,
No. 5 Quinsan Garden,
Shanghai.

Sir,

We, the residents in the apartments, after
consultation have decided to reject your demand
regarding the raising of house-rents, looking upon
the matter as of no reason.

The room-rents which we have been paying is
very dear in comparison with house-rents prevailing
in the Hongkew District, and we have not been
satisfied with your rents. We could not help tolerating
your rents because of the shortage of vacant houses but
after close investigation, we are hereby giving you our
just requirements and are asking for your re-consideration
to the carrying out of our requirements. We ask you
to accept whole our requirements in conformity with the
co-operation, of which you usually speak, while it is
necessary for all peoples, irrespective of nationality,
to co-operate for the goal to the establishment of New
Order in Asia.

Please answer to the letter within ten days.

From all Japanese residents
in the Quinsan Garden Apts.

The Office of the Japanese
Residents' Club of Quinsa..
Garden, Quinsan Apts.,
House No.4, Room No.11
Tel. 41134.

Tanaka Interpreter - Negotiator Service,
Range Road. Telephone No.46522.

译文。

1938年10月。

J... 利维先生，
上海昆山路花园5号。

先生，

我们公寓住户经协商后，决定拒绝您关于
提高房租的要求，认为该要求毫无道理。

与我们支付的房租相比，虹口地区通行的
房租要便宜得多，我们对您的租金一直不满意。
由于空置房屋短缺，我们不得不容忍您的租金，
但经过仔细调查，我们在此提出我们的合理要求，
并要求您重新考虑以落实我们的要求。我们请您
本着您通常所说的合作精神，接受我们的全部要求，
因为无论国籍如何，所有人都有必要为实现建立
亚洲新秩序的目标而合作。

请在十天内回复此信。

昆山路花园公寓全体
日本住户

昆山路花园日本
住户俱乐部办公室，
昆山路公寓，
4号房，11室

pages.en:
Requirements.

1. To charge the rent in Chinese Dollar. There have been two ways
of charging of rent, one in Japanese Yen, the other in
Chinese Dollar. There is no reason to charge so differently, so
it will be right to charge all rents in Chinese Dollar.

2. Regarding taking a bath.
Actually taking a bath is carried on every other day.
In view of the Japanese custom, it is desired by us for you
to revise so that a bath can be taken every day.

3. Regarding a watchman.
It is desired by us for you to employ a watchman to prevent
thefts, etc.

4. Regarding rooms and fixtures.
Ventilation in every room is bad now and fixtures are dirty and
damaged, which are wanted to be improved.

5. W.C.
Only one is used by several families, which is of the Chinese
fashion and consequently it is very dirty.
W.C. is desired to be of "water-washing" style (pumping style).

6. Regarding illumination.
Every house and its corridor are dark and dangerous, illumination
of which is desired to be improved.

7. Re telephone.
One telephone is desired to be installed at every house.

8. Regarding drying-place.
A drying-place is wanted to be provided with at every house.

9. Regarding reducing the rents.
The rents have been too dear. We cannot tolerate the high
rents. 50% is wanted to be reduced.
pages.zh:
要求。

1. 以中国元收取租金。目前收取租金有两种方式，一种以日元，另一种以中国元。如此区别收费并无理由，因此将所有租金均以中国元收取方为妥当。

2. 关于沐浴。
实际上目前是隔日沐浴一次。
鉴于日本习俗，我方希望贵方予以修改，以便能够每日沐浴。

3. 关于看守人。
我方希望贵方雇佣一名看守人，以防盗窃等事。

4. 关于房间及固定装置。
目前每个房间的通风状况不佳，且固定装置肮脏破损，亟需改善。

5. 厕所。
仅有一个厕所供数户家庭共用，且为中式风格，因此非常肮脏。
希望厕所改为“水冲式”（抽水式）。

6. 关于照明。
每栋房屋及其走廊光线昏暗且存在危险，希望改善照明。

7. 关于电话。
希望每栋房屋安装一部电话。

8. 关于晾晒处。
希望每栋房屋提供一处晾晒场所。

9. 关于降低租金。
租金过于昂贵。我们无法容忍高昂的租金。希望降低50%。

October 20th, 1939.

Report on complaint against D.I.S. 809 T. Masuda lodged by Mrs.
Samuel Goldstein, owner of "Rooming Houses" situated at Quinsan
Gardens.

Sir,
    On the afternoon of October 18th, 1939, Mr. H.H. Thomas,
Attaché for Japanese Affairs at F.B.N. Consulate telephoned the
Inspector in charge Hongkew to inform him that Mrs. Levy, owner
of "Rooming Houses" situated at Quinsan Gardens had a complaint
to make with reference to Japanese tenants, and was sending her
to the station to lodge it.
    Mrs. Samuel Goldstein, who is owner of the "Rooming Houses"
at Quinsan Gardens from No.1 to No.10 and as proprietrix of the
houses uses her maiden name Miss Lily Levy, about 3.30 p.m. on
October 18th, 1939 came to Hongkew Station with her mother, Mrs.
B.W. Levy, as per instructions from Mr. H.H. Thomas, and were
interviewed by the Inspector in charge and the undersigned.
They stated that a Japanese Mr. T. Masuda attached to the
Shanghai Municipal Police was in-stigating tenants not to
pay increase in rentals and also was seen putting up Japanese
flags outside the doorways of each house rented by them and
utilized as "Rooming Houses".
    Mrs. Samuel Goldstein was informed she would have to
make a statement duly signed by her with reference to the allega-
tions she made and it was arranged she would do so on the after-
noon of October 19th, 1939.
    As agreed she gave her statement on latter date
which was taken down by the undersigned and signed by her.
Same is attached, herewith, along with a circular notice and
two copies of letters written to Ki. T. Masuda in connection with
the rental increase.

1939年10月20日。

关于昆山路花园（Quinsan Gardens）“分租房屋”业主塞缪尔·戈德斯坦夫人（Mrs. Samuel Goldstein）对警务处巡捕 D.I.S. 809 T. Masuda 提出的投诉之报告。

先生：
    1939年10月18日下午，法国驻沪总领事馆（F.B.N. Consulate）日本事务专员 H.H. Thomas 先生致电虹口分区主管督察，告知昆山路花园“分租房屋”业主 Levy 夫人就日本租客一事有投诉欲提出，并正派其前往警局提交投诉。
    塞缪尔·戈德斯坦夫人是昆山路花园1号至10号“分租房屋”的业主，作为房产所有人，她使用其婚前姓名 Lily Levy 小姐。1939年10月18日下午约3时30分，她遵照 H.H. Thomas 先生的指示，与其母亲 B.W. Levy 夫人一同来到虹口警局，由主管督察及具名人进行了问询。
    她们陈述称，隶属于上海公共租界工部局警务处的一名日本人 T. Masuda 正在煽动租客拒付增加的租金，并且有人看见他在各栋被用作“分租房屋”出租的门口悬挂日本国旗。
    已告知塞缪尔·戈德斯坦夫人，她必须就其所指控的事项签署一份正式声明，并安排其于1939年10月19日下午办理此事。
    按约定，她在次日提交了声明，由具名人记录并经其签字确认。该声明现随函附上，另附一份通告以及两封就租金上涨事宜写给 T. Masuda 的信函副本。

- 2 -

T. Masuda, is has been ascertained, is D.P.S. 809
attached to wayside station. Attached also is a list of
**〔此处转录不清〕**, handed in by Mrs. J. Goldstein, giving
details of those who refuse to consider the increase.

It has been explained to the proprietrix of the
"Rooming Houses" that the Police could not take any particular
action as regards the tenants refusing to pay rentals owing to
the increase as it was purely a civil matter and as regards the
flag incident Mr. H.H. Thomas, Consul for Japanese Affairs at
Vancouver Consulate would deal with that complaint. However, she
has given the attached statement with reference to D.P.S. 809
T. Masuda's activities since the rentals were increased and has
been told same would be forwarded to Headquarters for considera-
tion.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

signed A. TELFER.

Det. Insp.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

经查实，T. Masuda 系隶属于路边警亭的警务处巡捕 D.P.S. 809。同时附上的还有 J. Goldstein 夫人提交的 **〔此处转录不清〕** 清单，详细列出了那些拒绝考虑涨租的人员。

已向该“分租房屋”的女业主解释，警方无法就租客因涨租而拒付租金一事采取任何具体行动，因为这纯属民事纠纷；至于悬挂国旗一事，温哥华领事馆（Vancouver Consulate）的日本事务领事 H.H. Thomas 先生将处理该投诉。然而，她就警务处巡捕 D.P.S. 809 T. Masuda 在租金上涨后的活动提交了所附声明，并已被告知该声明将呈送总部审议。

此致，
敬礼，

签名 A. TELFER.

侦探督察

TENANTS OF PEARCE APARTMENTS WILL REFUSE TO PAY
RENT

As already reported, the tenants of Pearce
Apartments on September 13 sent a strong protest to the
Shanghai Land Investment Company, Ltd., against the
unreasonable increase in rentals.

pages.en:
SHANGHAI EVENING POST & MERCURY
OCT 27 1939

No. S. R. D. ____
Date ____

Tenants Defying
Eviction Orders

Army Of 3000 Waging
Protracted Legal
Clash With Bank

The 15 month old legal battle between the Shanghai Women's Commercial and Savings Bank and the tenants of the Chingyuli alley a block of Chinese dwellings bordering Chengtu Chungking and Mandalay Road, was resumed in the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court this morning.

The main controversy in the case unlike the other landlord-tenant suits heard in Shanghai courts during the last few weeks was the bank's demand for eviction of the tenants from the 69 houses in which live more than 3000 persons. At the present stage of the legal battle, the tenants are the plaintiffs seeking to request the court to cancel a former judgment in favor of the bank.

Witnesses Questioned

This morning's hearing was devoted to the questioning of several witnesses in connection with an agreement allegedly binding the Women's Bank with the Shanghai Benevolent-Industrial Institution, from whom the bank had leased the land. The courtroom at Weihaiwei Road was again crowded by the anxious tenants whose future abode depends on the outcome of the case.

After a long session, Judges Y. J. Han, H. Shen and C. L. Tsang decided to adjourn the hearing since the Several points in the case, they ruled, must be ascertained before the counsels may proceed with pleadings and before a judgment could be given.

Protracted Battle

The protracted landlord-tenant legal battle was more than once featured by violent sideshows, including clashes between the tenants and the demolition gang sent to pull down the block of houses.

The legal battle was first started in July last year when the Shanghai Women's Commercial and Savings Bank instituted proceedings against the tenants, totalling some 3000 residents in all, asking for an eviction order. The bank contended that it had an agreement with the Shanghai Benevolent Industrial Institution, owners of the land, to rebuild the houses before the end of December, last year. The agreement, it was alleged, provides the payment of $200,000 damages for failing to carry out that stipulation. The First Special District Court rejected the application, whereupon the bank filed an appeal.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》
1939年10月27日

编号 S. R. D. ____
日期 ____

租客蔑视
驱逐令

三千人大军与银行
展开持久法律
冲突

上海女子商业储蓄银行与静安寺路（Chengtu Chungking，即成都路/重庆路区域，原文可能有误或指特定路段）、曼达礼路（Mandalay Road，即茂名路）交界处的一排中式住宅——静裕里（Chingyuli）的租客之间，持续了15个月的法律诉讼，今天上午在江苏高等法院第二分院重新开庭。

与过去几周上海法院审理的其他房东-租客诉讼不同，本案的主要争议点在于银行要求驱逐居住在69栋房屋中的3000多名租客。在目前的法律诉讼阶段，租客作为原告，请求法院撤销此前有利于银行的判决。

询问证人

今天上午的听证会主要用于询问几名证人，这些证人与一项据称约束女子银行与上海慈善工业社（Shanghai Benevolent-Industrial Institution）的协议有关，银行是从后者手中租赁的土地。威海卫路的法庭再次挤满了焦虑的租客，他们的未来住所取决于案件的结果。

经过长时间的庭审，法官韩义杰（Y. J. Han，音译）、沈某（H. Shen，音译）和曾某（C. L. Tsang，音译）决定休庭，因为他们裁定，在律师继续进行辩护和作出判决之前，必须查明案件中的几个要点。

持久战

这场持久的房东-租客法律斗争曾多次伴随激烈的插曲，包括租客与被派来拆除这片房屋的拆迁队之间的冲突。

这场法律斗争始于去年7月，当时上海女子商业储蓄银行对总计约3000名居民提起诉讼，要求发布驱逐令。银行辩称，它与土地所有者上海慈善工业社达成协议，要在去年12月底前重建房屋。据称，该协议规定，若未能履行该条款，需支付20万美元的赔偿金。第一特区法院驳回了该申请，随后银行提起上诉。

pages.en:
Clash With Wreckers

In the Second Branch Kiangsu
High Court, the bank won the
battle as a judgment was handed
down requiring the tenants to
evacuate before April 1 this year.
While the tenants were mustering
resources to turn the tide of the
legal battle the bank sent a de-
molition gang to start encircling
the houses with bamboo fences.
There were several clashes during
which several of the tenants were
charged in private criminal pro-
secutions by the bank. The
tenants were later acquitted.

A new turn in the suit took
place recently when the tenants
filed a fresh suit requesting a re-
trial of the case on the ground
that new evidence had been un-
earthed. An application for a
stay in the eviction order was also
made. The applications were
granted by the Special Branch
Kiangsu High Court.

Secret Agreement

The new evidence was in the
form of a secret agreement be-
tween the bank and the Shang-
hai Benevolent Industrial Institu-
tion, the tenants allege, which
provides that this block of houses
concerned must be rebuilt before
January 1, 1942, instead of Decem-
ber 31 1939, as previously contend-
ed by the bank. The agreement
also provides a reduction of the
land rental by 20 percent. The
tenants requested that the original
judgment ordering their eviction
be cancelled in view of the new
evidence and that the bank's re-
quest for their eviction be reject-
ed.

Attorneys Henry Y. A. Yuen
and Ginger Su appeared for the
tenants.
pages.zh:
与拆迁队的冲突

在江苏高等法院第二分院，银行赢得了这场官司，法院下达判决，要求租客在今年4月1日前搬离。当租客们集结资源以扭转法律诉讼的局面时，银行派遣了一支拆迁队开始用竹篱笆围住房屋。期间发生了几次冲突，银行对其中几名租客提起了私人刑事起诉。租客后来被宣告无罪。

最近，诉讼出现了新的转折，租客以发现新证据为由，提起新的诉讼，要求重审此案。同时还申请暂缓执行驱逐令。这些申请获得了江苏高等法院特别庭的批准。

秘密协议

租客声称，新证据的形式是银行与上海慈善工业社之间的一项秘密协议，该协议规定，涉案的这片房屋必须在1942年1月1日之前重建，而不是银行此前声称的1939年12月31日。该协议还规定地租减少20%。租客请求鉴于新证据，撤销命令其搬迁的原判决，并驳回银行的驱逐请求。

律师 Henry Y. A. Yuen（音译）和 Ginger Su（音译）代表租客出庭。

1939年10月23日

租客诉
房东案

泰勒夫人的诉讼未被驳回，而是发回修改

在本刊昨日刊登的关于第二区法院审理 Brookside 公寓租客 J. Taylor 夫人对房东 Peter K. C. Li 先生提起的民事诉讼程序的报道中，错误地报道该诉讼已被驳回。法院的裁决是该诉讼应发回，以便提交经修正的诉状。
在此更正之际，需要指出的是，中国第二区法院从未审理过泰勒夫人的案件，而只是（无论正确与否）提出了某些程序性问题。由于误解，泰勒夫人及其律师均未出席第一次听证会，而另一位租客 J. S. Chisholm 先生基于相同理由对 Peter Li 先生提起的类似诉讼则获得了成功。

（手写批注：）
Li.
C.S.

pages.en:
CHINA PRESS.

OCT 23 1939

15-Month-Old Landlord-Tenant
Dispute Again Heard In Court

Judges Asked To Put Off Eviction Order Granted
To Women's Bank In Earlier Litigation

Another attempt to retain pos-
session was made yesterday by
tenants of a block of Chinese
dwellings on Chengtu Road as
legal battle began anew in the
Second Branch Kiangsu High Court
seeking to set aside an earlier judg-
ment ordering the eviction of the
tenants.

The new proceedings were in-
stituted by the tenants on the
ground that a secret agreement had
existed between the defendant,
owner of the houses, and the lessor
of the land, the revelation of which,
the complainants contended, would
have invalidated the owner's argu-
ment in the earlier case.

It was pointed out that the
owner, the Shanghai Women's
Commercial and Savings Bank, won
the earlier litigation largely on the
ground that under a contract with
the land owners, they were to re-
build the houses prior to Decem-
ber 31, 1939, or to pay $200,000
damages.

New Contract Alleged

The alleged secret contract pro-
vides, the complainants said, that
the rebuilding may not take place
before January 1, 1942 and that the
land rental be reduced by 20 per
cent. The owners of the land are
the Shanghai Benevolent Industrial
Institution.

At yesterday's hearing, a few
witnesses were admitted by the
Court to testify for the complain-
ants. They stated that evidence
of the contract came to their
knowledge after the conclusion of
the previous litigation between the
same parties.

The adjournment of the case was
ordered by the presiding judges,
Messrs Y. J. Han, H. Shen and C.
L. Tsang, in view of the fact, they
stated, that several points must be
ascertained before the parties can
proceed with their pleadings.

The dispute between the bank
and the tenants began in July last
year when suit was instituted by the
bank for the recovery of the pos-
session of the premises from the
tenants.

Bank Loses Suit

In the Civil Branch of the Second
Special District Court, the bank
failed to obtain satisfaction and
the case was subsequently taken to
the high court where judgment was
found in its favor and the tenants
were ordered to be evicted.

A series of incidents followed as
a result of this order when the
tenants refused to give up their
possession. Several times, the
bank despatched wrecking gangs
to the area and attempted to pull
down the dwellings by force. They
also sought to disconnect the water
and light lines running into the
area. Each time, the bank failed
as the tenants in an organized way
gave resistance to the workmen.

Early this month, the com-
plainants applied to the high court
for a new trial of the case, which
application was granted.

《字林西报》。

1939年10月23日

历时15个月的房东与租客纠纷
再次在法庭审理

法官被请求推迟执行早前诉讼中
判给女子商业储蓄银行的驱逐令

昨日，随着法律战在江苏高等法院第二分院重新打响，成都路上一片中式住宅的租户再次尝试保留占有权，试图推翻早前命令驱逐租户的判决。

新诉讼由租户提起，理由是被告（即房屋业主）与土地出租人之间存在一项秘密协议，原告方声称，该协议的披露将使业主在前案中的论点无效。

有人指出，业主上海女子商业储蓄银行之所以赢得前次诉讼，主要依据是与土地所有者签订的一份合同，根据该合同，他们须在1939年12月31日前重建房屋，否则需支付20万美元的赔偿金。

指称存在新合同

原告方称，据称存在的秘密合同规定，重建工作不得早于1942年1月1日进行，且地租减少20%。土地所有者为上海慈善工业社（Shanghai Benevolent Industrial Institution）。

在昨日的听证会上，法院准许几名证人为原告作证。他们表示，关于该合同的证据是在同一双方之前的诉讼结束后才为他们所知的。

主审法官韩义杰（Y. J. Han）、沈某（H. Shen）和曾某（C. L. Tsang）下令休庭，他们表示，鉴于在双方继续进行诉辩之前必须查明若干要点。

银行与租户之间的纠纷始于去年7月，当时银行提起诉讼，要求从租户手中收回房产的占有权。

银行败诉

在第二特区地方法院民事庭，银行未能获得满意结果，案件随后上诉至高等法院，法院作出有利于银行的判决，并命令驱逐租户。

由于该命令，随后发生了一系列事件，租户拒绝放弃占有权。银行多次派遣拆迁队前往该地区，试图强行拆除住宅。他们还试图切断通往该地区的水电线路。每次银行都未能成功，因为租户有组织地抵抗工人作业。

本月初，原告向高等法院申请重审此案，该申请获准。

NORTH CHINA DAILY NEWS
OCT 27 1939
211

Mr. J. S. Chisholm Defendant
In Rent Case in H.M. Court

Local Tenancies Subject to Chinese Law Unless
Other Laws Imported Into Contracts

HIS Lordship expressed the hope that the two parties would be able to reach a compromise before the resumption of the hearing in which Mr. Peter Li, owner of the Brookside Apartments, represented by Mr. U. A. Reeks, asked for the recovery of apartment 4 G, occupied by Mr. J. S. Chisholm, prominent member of the Shanghai Tenants Association, represented by Mr. John McNeill, when the case came up for hearing before Judge Sir Allan Mossop in H.M. Supreme Court yesterday morning.

Counsel for the plaintiff, in placing his case before the court, stated that a lease on the said premises had been drawn up between the two parties on August 12, 1938 and came into force on October 1, 1938. It expired on October 1 of this year and, although the defendant was informed of the fact that the lease would not be renewed, a letter to that effect having been addressed to him on September 12, by Mr. Elliott Hazzard, agent for the owner of the building, Mr. Chisholm was still in occupation and had refused to vacate the apartment on October 1. Plaintiff, therefore, demanded recovery of the premises and mesne profits from October 1 until the day on which Mr. Chisholm would move out, on the basis of a monthly rental of $185.

The only witness to testify yesterday was Mr. Hazzard, who said that he had given instructions to Messrs. Ellis & Hays to request Mr. Chisholm to vacate the premises at the expiration of the lease. A letter was accordingly sent on September 12, and in reply to a question by Mr. McNeill, witness said that the contents of the letter met with his approval.

Mr. McNeill:—Did you give instructions to commence these proceedings?
Mr. Hazzard:—I told them to take all the steps necessary in pursuance of the contents of the letter.
Mr. McNeill:—Are any monies due to the landlords from Mr. Chisholm for months previous to October?
Mr. Hazzard:—There is a small balance due, but not on the basis of $185.
Mr. McNeill:—Why is not that money claimed on the writ?
Mr. Hazzard:—I don't know, but it is a very small balance.
Mr. Hazzard then explained that the small balance had arisen as a result of the introduction of a new monthly rent on the basis of U.S. $25 as from August 1, 1939.
Mr. McNeill:—Is there anything contained in the lease which, during its validity, permits an increase in rent?—No.
Witness then stated that the balance had arisen out of the difference between the old rental of $185 and the new rental of U.S. $36, of which amount one half was to be paid at the exchange of 16 cents U.S. currency to $1, whereas the other half was to be paid at the rate of exchange of the day of payment. The lease, he added, was cancelled on June 26, cancellation taking effect on August 1.
Mr. McNeill then asked the court how plaintiff could found his action on an expired lease and asked for judgment.
In referring to the cancellation, Mr. Reeks said that defendant took action in the Chinese court which ruled that this lease could not be cancelled by one month's notice.
Mr. McNeill (to Mr. Hazzard):—I think the position is clear. The lease has either been cancelled or it has not been cancelled properly.
Mr. Reeks:—This is a question of law.

Question of Common Sense

Mr. McNeill:—No, this is a question of common sense. Your writ assumes that it is not cancelled. I think that you will agree that if the lease is not cancelled, you are not entitled to charge additional rent for the months of August and September.
Mr. Hazzard:—No. There is no claim against Mr. Chisholm over and above $185 if the lease is not cancelled.

Asked by Mr. McNeill whether the defendant had paid Mr. Hazzard $195 both in August and September, the additional $10 being for the use of a refrigerator, Mr. Hazzard answered in the affirmative.

It was then revealed that Mr. Chisholm had received a rental advice on October 1, and had sent a cheque to Mr. Hazzard the following day, amounting to $195.

Mr. McNeill:—That cheque was cashed?—Yes.
Mr. McNeill:—Why did you send Mr. Chisholm another rental advice notice on October 1, if you wanted him to move out?—Because there was another action pending.
Mr. McNeill:—Assuming that the lease is uncancelled, this $195 represents the rental for October?—Presumably, under this assumption.
Mr. McNeill:—Assuming that the lease was cancelled, you still sent Mr. Chisholm a debit note for October and therefore you were still willing to have him as a tenant?
His Lordship:—Under a new tenancy, don't forget.
Mr. McNeill:—Let me repeat my question. When you presented your debit note for October, you were prepared to have Mr. Chisholm as a tenant at the increased rent?—For the one month.
Mr. McNeill:—Were you prepared to let Mr. Chisholm have a lease on a month to month basis on the new, increased rental?—My instructions were not to do it. He was merely there for October because he would not get out.

In reply to a question, Mr. Hazzard admitted that a cheque for $195 had been sent to Mr. Chisholm by him on October 12 and that he knew that this cheque had been returned to his solicitors.

At this point, witness made reference to a letter dated July 10, which however, neither Mr. Reeks nor Mr. McNeill could trace in their papers, whereupon Mr. Reeks said:

（右侧手写批注：Li C）

《华北每日新闻》
1939年10月27日
211

J. S. Chisholm 先生成为
英皇陛下法院租金案被告

除非合同中引入其他法律，否则本地租赁受中国法律管辖

昨天上午，当案件在英皇陛下最高法院由阿兰·莫索普爵士（Sir Allan Mossop）法官审理时，法官表示希望双方能在听证会恢复前达成妥协。听证会涉及布鲁克赛德公寓（Brookside Apartments）业主彼得·李（Peter Li）先生（由 U. A. Reeks 律师代表）要求收回由上海租户协会知名成员 J. S. Chisholm 先生（由 John McNeill 律师代表）占用的4G室公寓。

原告律师在向法庭陈述案情时表示，双方于1938年8月12日就上述物业签订了租约，并于1938年10月1日生效。租约于今年10月1日到期，尽管已通知被告租约不再续期——大楼业主代理人 Elliott Hazzard 先生已于9月12日致函告知此事——但 Chisholm 先生仍占据该公寓，并拒绝于10月1日搬离。因此，原告要求收回物业，并按每月185美元的租金标准，索取从10月1日起至 Chisholm 先生搬离之日止的中间利润（mesne profits）。

昨日作证的唯一证人是 Hazzard 先生，他表示已指示 Ellis & Hays 律师事务所要求在租约期满时请 Chisholm 先生腾退物业。因此于9月12日发出了一封信件，在回答 McNeill 先生的提问时，证人表示信件内容得到了他的批准。

McNeill 先生：——您是否指示启动这些诉讼程序？
Hazzard 先生：——我告诉他们采取一切必要步骤，以落实信件内容。
McNeill 先生：——Chisholm 先生是否欠房东10月之前几个月的任何款项？
Hazzard 先生：——有一笔小额欠款，但并非基于185美元的标准。
McNeill 先生：——为何传票中未索赔这笔钱？
Hazzard 先生：——我不知道，但这笔余额很小。
Hazzard 先生随后解释说，这笔小额余额是由于自1939年8月1日起引入了基于25美元的新月租而产生的。
McNeill 先生：——租约有效期内是否有任何条款允许增加租金？——没有。
证人随后表示，余额产生于旧租金185美元与新租金36美元之间的差额，其中一半按1美元兑换16美分的汇率支付，另一半按付款当日汇率支付。他补充说，租约于6月26日取消，8月1日生效。
McNeill 先生随即询问法庭，原告如何能基于一份已过期的租约提起诉讼，并要求作出判决。
谈及取消事宜时，Reeks 先生表示，被告在中国法院采取了行动，该法院裁定该租约不能通过一个月通知予以取消。
McNeill 先生（对 Hazzard 先生说）：——我认为情况很清楚。租约要么已被取消，要么未被properly取消。
Reeks 先生：——这是一个法律问题。

常识问题

McNeill 先生：——不，这是一个常识问题。您的传票假设租约未被取消。我想您会同意，如果租约未被取消，您无权就8月和9月收取额外租金。
Hazzard 先生：——不。如果租约未被取消，除185美元外，对 Chisholm 先生没有其他索赔。

当 McNeill 先生询问被告是否在8月和9月均向 Hazzard 先生支付了195美元，其中额外的10美元是冰箱使用费时，Hazzard 先生给予了肯定回答。

随后透露，Chisholm 先生于10月1日收到了一份租金通知单，并于次日向 Hazzard 先生发送了一张金额为195美元的支票。

McNeill 先生：——那张支票兑现了吗？——是的。
McNeill 先生：——如果您希望他搬走，为何在10月1日又给 Chisholm 先生发了一份租金通知单？——因为还有另一起诉讼 pending。
McNeill 先生：——假设租约未取消，这195美元代表10月份的租金吗？——在此假设下， presumably 是的。
McNeill 先生：——假设租约已取消，您仍向 Chisholm 先生发送了10月份的借记单，因此您仍愿意让他作为租户？
法官大人：——别忘了，是在新租约下。
McNeill 先生：——让我重复我的问题。当您提交10月份的借记单时，您准备让 Chisholm 先生以增加的租金作为租户吗？——仅针对那一个月。
McNeill 先生：——您是否准备让 Chisholm 先生按月租赁，并按新的、增加的租金执行？——我的指示是不这样做。他仅仅因为不肯搬走而在那里待过10月份。

在回答一个问题时，Hazzard 先生承认他于10月12日向 Chisholm 先生发送了一张195美元的支票，并且他知道这张支票已被退回给他的律师。

此时，证人提及一封日期为7月10日的信件，然而 Reeks 先生和 McNeill 先生均无法在他们的文件中找到该信，于是 Reeks 先生说：

（右侧手写批注：Li C）

pages.en:
Compromise Said Offered
Here is all the correspondence I
have, except the letter which was
received from Mr. Chisholm a few
minutes before the opening of the
hearing.
Mr. Chisholm, sitting behind his
solicitor, was then heard saying that
the letter had nothing to do with the
case.
Mr. Reeks: Nothing? It is a letter
asking for a compromise.
A little later Mr. McNeill stated
that his client was prepared to pay
a higher rental. As a matter of fact,
a substantial increase on the previous
rental but that he refused to pay it
in a foreign currency.
His Lordship: I appreciate the
difference in opinion.
Mr. Reeks then pointed out that
with the exception of some 20 ten-
ants, all the other residents of Brook-
side Apartments were paying the
new rental which, Mr. Reeks pointed
out, was very reasonable indeed.
Mr. McNeill then asked for an ad-
journment and said that, in the mean-
time, he would file an application,
asking the court to fix a reasonable
and fair rental for the premises.
After pointing out that Chinese
law applied to these tenancies unless
some other law was imported into
the contract, His Lordship said that
he could not see why all these letters
had been exchanged when an applica-
tion under paragraph 442 of the
Chinese Civil Code might have been
made for an increase in rentals. In
adjourning the hearing, His Lord-
ship said that nothing would please
him more than to hear that the two
parties had reached an agreement
before the date of the next hearing.

这是我所有的往来信件，除了

Reeks 先生：无关？这是一封

稍后，McNeill 先生表示，他的

Reeks 先生随后指出，除了大约

Reeks 先生指出，这确实非常合

SHANGHAI TIMES
OCT 2

Civil Action Against Mr.
Peter Li Dismissed

British Complainant, Mrs. J. Taylor, Is Not Upheld
in Contention Advanced That Landlord Has
No Right To Evict, Claim High Rent

The Second Special District Court yesterday dismissed the civil action filed by Mrs. J. Taylor, a tenant of the Bredene Apartments, against her landlord, Mr. Peter K. C. Li, in which complainant contended that defendant had no right to evict her, and that payment of rent should not be made in French Franc currency.

Mr. Taylor had entered into a contractual agreement with the landlord for the lease of the apartment mentioned, and under the terms of the contract the landlord could not ask her to vacate the premises until the contract expired on October 1, 1940. The landlord could not demand payment of rental in American currency because Mr. Taylor maintained that he had stipulated in the contract that rental is fixed at Ch.$175 per month. Mr. Li had notified her that commencing from August 1, 1939 rental would be collected at U.S.$32 per month. By having to pay the rental in American currency, complainant contended she would have to pay actually Ch.$450 per month, or sustain a clear loss of nearly Ch.$275 each month.

**Appeal Dismissed**

Mrs. Taylor had previously filed an appeal at the Third Branch Kiangsu High Court, but Judge Hsia dismissed the appeal and sustained the contentions of Mr. Li whose counsel, Mr. T. C. Chen, maintained that under a supplementary clause in the contract, both landlord and tenant could give notice of eviction or to vacate the premises one month beforehand.

On June 26, Mr. Li wrote Mrs. Taylor informing her that the rental would be collected at U.S. $32 per month. This letter, Mr. Chen contended, was in the nature of an offer, and since Mrs. Taylor did not reply to it, Mr. Chen declared, there was no acceptance. On this ground Mr. Li could seek the eviction of the tenant, he maintained.

M. D'Auxion de Ruffe and Mr. Tcheou Liang-fou, for the appellant, contended that the letter of June 26 was followed by another letter dated August 4, in which the landlord threatened to take action against their client in the British Court for China. To make a new offer while the contract had clearly stipulated that the lease would be valid until October 1, 1940, was clearly contrary to the terms of the contract, appellant's counsels maintained.

On October 5, Judge Hsia dismissed the case in favour of Mr. Peter K. C. Li.

In the Second Special District Court yesterday, Mrs. Taylor filed a civil suit against the landlord. But the Court authorities refused to countenance the suit, declaring that it had no authority to revoke the decision of a higher tribunal.

《字林西报》
10月2日

针对彼得·李先生的民事诉讼被驳回

英国原告J.泰勒夫人关于房东无权驱逐租客、索要高额租金的主张未获支持

第二特区地方法院昨日驳回了布雷登公寓（Bredene Apartments）租户J.泰勒夫人对其房东彼得·K·C·李先生提起的民事诉讼。原告在诉讼中主张，被告无权将其驱逐，且租金不应以法国法郎货币支付。

泰勒先生已与房东就上述公寓的租赁签订了合同协议，根据合同条款，在合同于1940年10月1日到期之前，房东不得要求其搬离该处所。房东不能要求以美元支付租金，因为泰勒先生坚持认为，他在合同中规定租金固定为每月国币175元。李先生曾通知她，自1939年8月1日起，租金将按每月32美元收取。原告主张，由于必须以美元支付租金，她实际上每月需支付国币450元，即每月遭受近国币275元的明显损失。

**上诉被驳回**

泰勒夫人此前曾向江苏高等法院第三分院提起上诉，但夏法官驳回了该上诉，并维持了李先生的主张。李先生的代理律师陈T.C.先生坚持认为，根据合同中的补充条款，房东和租客均可提前一个月发出驱逐或搬离该处所的通知。

6月26日，李先生致信泰勒夫人，告知其租金将按每月32美元收取。陈先生主张，这封信的性质是一项要约，而由于泰勒夫人未予回复，陈先生宣称，因此不存在承诺。据此，他坚持认为李先生可以寻求驱逐该租户。

代表上诉人的D'Auxion de Ruffe先生和周良甫（音译）先生主张，6月26日的信件之后还有另一封 dated 8月4日的信件，房东在信中威胁要对他们的当事人在英国在华法院提起诉讼。上诉人的律师坚持认为，在合同明确规定租约有效期至1940年10月1日的情况下提出新的要约，显然违反了合同条款。

10月5日，夏法官作出了有利于彼得·K·C·李先生的判决，驳回了此案。

昨日，泰勒夫人在第二特区地方法院对房东提起民事诉讼。但法院当局拒绝受理该诉讼，宣称其无权撤销上级法庭的裁决。
